messages:
customer-rep-jdoe: heads up — three customers (one enterprise) reporting 502s to Hosted API around 2025-03-17 12:28-12:34 PST. attaching two trace ids: abc123 and def456. they call the /v1/generate endpoint, non-streaming.

maria (support): thanks — any repro curl or client samples? are these from the same region?

customer-rep-jdoe: all NA-west clients. sample curl from one customer:
```bash
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
```
response: HTTP/2 502, server: envoy, x-trace-id: abc123

alex (eng-sre): looking at frontdoor logs for abc123 — seeing repeated `upstream reset` and `upstream premature close` from midproxy cluster. snippet:
```
[2025-03-17T19:28:15Z] trace=abc123 level=error envoy upstream reset: connection closed before response headers
[2025-03-17T19:28:15Z] trace=abc123 midproxy: pool saturation, queued requests=120
```

jon (ingress): corroborating — our envoy metrics show burst of concurrent h2 streams, keepalive pools exhausted. interestingly the auth cache had a synchronized refresh at approx 12:27:59 PST (billing sync kicked off). might be correlated.

lisa (oncall): priority — customer impact. immediate mitigations: 1) enable fallback-route for hostedapi -> dedicated-pool for affected tenants 2) temporarily raise midproxy conn cap 3) roll back billing sync if possible. can ops perform 1 & 2?

maria (support): I informed customers and opened a ticket: #INC-99821. asked them for exact request sizes; one was 2.1MB payload, others small.

ops-bot: created incident INC-99821, notify @oncall.

alex (eng-sre): quick repro steps for infra team:
1) replay client's request at scale (100 concurrent) with `--http2`
2) watch midproxy `h2_streams_active` and `conn_pool_in_use`
3) check auth-cache hit ratio around rotation window

sample replay command:
```bash
seq 1 100 | xargs -n1 -P20 -I{} curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}' >/dev/null
```

jon (ingress): confirmed that bumping the midproxy connection pool + enabling the fallback-route reduced 502 rate to near zero for a test tenant. rolling these changes to prod now.

lisa (oncall): good — keep monitoring for 30m, then follow up with customers. also add an alert for auth-cache-refresh hot window + high queue depth so we can auto-scale earlier next time.

maria (support): customers updated. one said they saw immediate improvement. closing loop when monitoring stable. :thumbsup:
